note: Either Charles Martel's wife, Clemence of Habsburg, or their daughter of the same name, who became queen of France. "Your Charles" suits a wife better, but she was dead by the time Dante wrote. Readers remain divided.

context: The speaker of Canto 8, named only here, and only by his first name.

quote: the betrayals his descendants would suffer
note: When Charles II died in 1309, the crown of Naples went to his younger son Robert and not to Charles Martel's son, who had the elder claim.
God, the light that fills every soul in Heaven.

context: Dante looks to her for leave before he speaks, as he did in Canto 8.

quote: what I think can be reflected in you
note: The blessed see Dante's thoughts in the mind of God, so he need not ask his question aloud. He wants to know who she is.
The March of Treviso, the mainland behind Venice. The Rialto is the chief island of Venice, and the Brenta and Piave rise in the Alps to the north.

quote: a hill of no great height
note: The hill of Romano, with the castle of the family that took its name.

context: Her brother. The story went that before his birth his mother dreamed she was bringing forth a burning torch that set the whole region alight.
The tyrant's sister is in Heaven while he boils in Hell. Her place among the blessed has surprised readers from the first, and Dante seems to expect it.

note: She was ruled by the influence of Venus: she lived for love.
She does not grieve over her past. The same loving nature that led her astray brought her, once turned to God, to this heaven. Folco says more at line 104.
The soul beside her, who speaks next and names himself at line 95.
The century year 1300, when the journey takes place. It will come round five more times before his fame fades: a way of saying it will last for centuries.
The rivers on the western and eastern edges of the March of Treviso. Cunizza now foretells three disasters for her homeland. All had happened by the time Dante wrote.

Usually read as the defeat of Guelph Padua near Vicenza in 1314 by Cangrande della Scala, lord of Verona and the Emperor's deputy, who was later Dante's host and patron. The water is the river Bacchiglione, which flows past Vicenza.

quote: where the Sile and Cagnano meet
note: Treviso, where the two rivers join. Its lord was Rizzardo da Camino, who was murdered in 1312: the net is the plot against him.

Feltre, a town in the hills north of Treviso. In 1314 its bishop, Alessandro Novello, gave up a group of men from Ferrara who had taken refuge with him. They were handed to the governor of Ferrara and beheaded.
A prison called Malta, probably one where the popes held criminal clergy. Several places had the name, and it is not certain which Dante meant.
Bitter irony. The bishop made a present of his guests' lives to please the Guelph party.
One of the nine orders of angels. They reflect God's judgments like mirrors, and Cunizza reads the coming punishments in them. That is why such harsh words can be spoken in Heaven.
The second soul, the "jewel" Cunizza pointed out.
In Hell, where the shades grow darker as their minds grow sadder. In Heaven joy shows as more light, as on earth it shows as a smile.

context: Isaiah saw them covering themselves with their wings as they sang "Holy, holy, holy". The soul's voice joins in their song.

quote: if I dwelt in you as you dwell in me
note: Dante invents two verbs here: "s'io m'intuassi, come tu t'inmii", roughly "if I in-you'd myself as you in-me yourself". Ordinary language has no words for the way minds lie open to one another in Heaven, so he makes them.

The Mediterranean, the largest sea after the Ocean that was thought to ring all the land. Geographers of the time believed it ran a quarter of the way round the globe from west to east, so that the sun stood overhead at one end while it sat on the horizon at the other.

quote: between the Ebro and the Magra
note: The Ebro is in Spain, and the Magra reaches the sea near La Spezia in Italy. Marseille lies about halfway along the coast between them.
Béjaïa, on the coast of Algeria, almost due south of Marseille. The two share nearly the same hours of sunrise and sunset.

quote: made the harbor hot with blood
note: Marseille sided with Pompey in the civil war, and Julius Caesar's forces took it in 49 BC after a siege and a bloody sea battle, told by the poet Lucan.

context: Dante admired his love songs and quotes one in his treatise on writing poetry in the common tongue.

note: In life Venus stamped him with a lover's nature. Now his light is part of the planet's own.

context: Her love for Aeneas wronged her dead husband, Sichaeus, to whom she had sworn to be faithful, and the memory of Creusa, the wife Aeneas lost at Troy.

note: Phyllis, a princess of Thrace, the land of Mount Rhodope. Her lover Demophoon, son of Theseus, promised to come back and marry her. When he did not, she hanged herself. The story is in Ovid.
His passion for the princess Iole made his wife, Deianira, jealous. She sent him a robe smeared with what she thought was a love charm. It was poison, and it killed him.

Before entering Heaven every soul drinks from Lethe, the river at the top of Purgatory that washes away the memory of sin as guilt (Purgatorio 31). What remains is gladness at how God turned their nature to good.

context: A prostitute holds the highest rank in the heaven of the lovers. Christian writers saw in her a figure of the Church, saved from among the pagans.

note: Astronomers of the time taught that the earth's shadow stretches into space as a cone and comes to a point at the sphere of Venus. The souls of the three lowest heavens were marked by an earthly weakness: broken vows, love of fame, passion. Above here that shadow is gone.
The Harrowing of Hell. After his death Christ went down to Limbo and led out the souls of the just who had lived before him (Inferno 4). Rahab was the first of them to be received into this heaven.
His two hands, nailed to the cross.

context: His "first glorious deed" was the taking of Jericho, which Rahab made possible by hiding his spies.
Acre, the last Christian city in the Holy Land, fell in 1291, and no crusade followed. Boniface made war on his Christian enemies in Italy instead (Inferno 27).

quote: who first turned his back on his Maker
note: Satan, the first rebel, whose envy of mankind brought about the Fall. Folco calls Florence his planting.

The florin, the gold coin of Florence, first struck in 1252 and stamped with the city's lily. It became the standard money of Europe. Greed for it, Folco says, has turned the clergy from shepherds into wolves.

Dante's word is the Decretals, the collected rulings of the popes that made up Church law. Its study led to rich careers. The margins show it: those books are worn and crowded with notes, while the Gospels and the Church Fathers lie unread.
The town in Galilee where the angel came to Mary. It stands here for the Holy Land, now in Muslim hands and forgotten by the Church's leaders.
The hill in Rome where Peter was buried. In Dante's time it was revered as a burial ground of martyrs. The popes had long lived across the city at the Lateran.

context: His soldiers are the early Christians martyred in Rome.

quote: shall soon be freed from this adultery
note: The Church is the bride of Christ, and popes who love money are unfaithful to her. What rescue Folco foretells is left dark: suggestions include the death of Boniface in 1303, the move of the popes to Avignon soon after, and a reformer still to come.
